core_idea: **While** either points to a period of time during which something else happens, or joins two facts that go against each other.

senses.definition: during the time that something is happening
senses.explanation: A **while** clause points to a period of time, often with a continuous verb, during which the action in the main clause happens. It can come first, with a comma after it, or after the main clause, with no comma. When both clauses have the same subject, the clause can be shortened to an **-ing** form (*while driving*) or a phrase (*while at work*).

examples.text: While you were out, Ana called.
I read a book while I waited for the bus.
Don't use your phone while driving.
examples.note: with an **-ing** form and no subject

examples.text: Someone stole her bag while she was asleep.

compare.note: **while** stresses that two things go on at the same time; **when** simply names the time
**as** also joins two actions that happen at the same time, often short ones

senses.definition: used to set one fact against another fact that is different or surprising
senses.explanation: Used to link two facts that go against each other, without suggesting that one causes the other.

examples.text: While I understand your point, I don't agree.
The north is cold, while the south stays warm all year.
Sara enjoys cities, while her brother prefers the countryside.

synonyms.note: **whereas** is more formal and used mainly for contrast, never for time

adaptation.semantic: This contrastive use is unrelated to time; a translator should not automatically reach for the word for **during** here.

learner_errors.incorrect: While she will cook, I will clean.
learner_errors.correct: While she cooks, I will clean.
learner_errors.note: A **while** clause about the present or future normally uses the present tense, not **will**.

learner_errors.incorrect: During I was waiting, it started to rain.
learner_errors.correct: While I was waiting, it started to rain.
learner_errors.note: **During** is a preposition and goes before a noun (*during the wait*); before a clause with a subject and verb, use **while**.

see_also.note: the more general word for a contrast
the noun, a period of time (*a while*, *worth your while*)
